title: Unbounded ordinary etale compact-support comparisons
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and work on the small etale sites with constant-ring module sheaves and unbounded derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. All schemes below are Noetherian, meaning they admit finite affine covers by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Each morphism to which $R(-)_!$ is applied is separated and of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and has a compactification [def-asd-compactifiable]. For $c=(j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X,r:\overline X\to Y)$ put $Rf_!^c=Rr_*Dj_!$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support].

The proper-refinement comparisons, restricting to the identity on $X$, are canonical natural isomorphisms between these functors. Identity refinements give identities and composites give composites; comparison through a common refinement is independent of that refinement and satisfies the cocycle identity. Write $Rf_!$ for the resulting compactification-independent functor. For composable $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}Z$ there is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$\alpha_{g,f}:Rg_!Rf_!\xrightarrow{\sim}R(gf)_!,$$
independent of compactification choices, compatible with refinement comparisons and identities, and associative for three morphisms. Its normalization is the proper/open tower comparison: choose $Y\xrightarrow{i}\overline Y\xrightarrow{s}Z$ and $X\xrightarrow{a}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}\overline Y$ compactifying $g$ and $if$, respectively, put $V=\overline X\times_{\overline Y}Y$, and write $b:V\hookrightarrow\overline X$, $q:V\to Y$, $j:X\hookrightarrow V$, so $bj=a$. Then $\alpha_{g,f}$ is $Rs_*$ of the proper/open interchange $Di_!Rq_*\to Rp_*Db_!$, followed by the direct-image and open-extension composition identifications [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition, lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition]. The interchange is adjoint under $Di_!\dashv i^*$ to the inverse of the proper open-restriction exchange $i^*Rp_*\cong Rq_*b^*$, with $b^*Db_!\cong1$ [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality].

For a cartesian square [def-pc-fibre-product] with $f:X\to Y$, $v:Y'\to Y$, $X'=X\times_Y Y'$, and projections $v':X'\to X$, $f':X'\to Y'$, the natural exchange
$$C_{f,v}:v^*Rf_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_!v'^*$$
is an isomorphism on every unbounded complex. On a chosen compactification it is the canonical proper exchange [def-kun-unbounded-exchange], followed by the inverse of the degreewise open-extension comparison [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map]. It is independent of compactification, compatible with identities, composite changes of base and the composition comparisons $\alpha$. The comparisons and exchanges restrict on bounded-below inputs to those of [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons, thm-cbc-finite-torsion] with these same normalizations.

proof.text:
First fix the structural comparisons that will be inserted in all formulas. By [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] and [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], open extension and constant-module inverse image are exact, hence act termwise on every complex. The sheaf open adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] induces the termwise adjunction on homotopy categories by [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy]. Its unit and counit descend by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], since both functors are exact; their triangle identities descend as equalities. Hence $Dj_!\dashv j^*$ on the unbounded derived categories for every open immersion, without needing a finite-type hypothesis. The open composition and identity maps of [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition] consequently descend, with their same equations, by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. For proper maps use the canonical unbounded direct-image comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. Its associativity and units can be checked under the inverse-image/direct-image adjunctions specified in [def-kun-unbounded-exchange]: for three maps $a,b,c$, both comparisons are adjoint to the composite evaluation
$$a^*b^*c^*Rc_*Rb_*Ra_*\xrightarrow{a^*b^*\varepsilon_c}a^*b^*Rb_*Ra_*\xrightarrow{a^*\varepsilon_b}a^*Ra_*\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_a}1.$$
Termwise inverse-image composition identifies the two parenthesizations. The mate-pasting identities and identity clause of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] therefore give the same right-adjoint comparisons. They also show that proper exchange commutes with composition of proper maps and successive changes of base: take the mates of the pasted inverse-image square isomorphisms. This establishes the structural coherence used below on the entire derived categories.

proof.text: Use [lem-amb-unbounded-proper-open-interchange] for a square $Q=(U\xrightarrow{k}V,r,p,W\xrightarrow{i}Z)$ with open horizontal maps and proper vertical maps. Denote its specified isomorphism by $\Gamma_Q:Di_!Rr_*\to Rp_*Dk_!$. This is available on all of $D(U_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, including for noncartesian refinement squares. For a cartesian square the same node fixes its adjunct to be the inverse proper open-restriction exchange followed by the open unit identification. Thus this is precisely the tower normalization required in the statement, rather than an arbitrary isomorphism of the two functors. Retain both pasting identities and the base-change equation of this node throughout the construction.

For a refinement $u:c_1\to c_2$, write $c_i=(j_i,r_i)$, so $u j_1=j_2$ and $r_2u=r_1$. Apply $\Gamma$ to the square with top $j_1$, bottom $j_2$, and vertical maps $1_X,u$. It gives $\gamma_u:Dj_{2!}\to Ru_*Dj_{1!}$. For the candidates of [def-amb-etale-compact-support] define
$$\tau_u: F_{c_2}=Rr_{2,*}Dj_{2!}\xrightarrow{Rr_{2,*}\gamma_u}Rr_{2,*}Ru_*Dj_{1!}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rr_{1,*}Dj_{1!}=F_{c_1}.$$
It is a natural isomorphism by [lem-amb-unbounded-proper-open-interchange] and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. On the open $X$ the sheaf identification in $\gamma_u$ is the identity. The vertical pasting identity for $\Gamma$ gives $\gamma_{vu}=(Rv_*\gamma_u)\gamma_v$ for $u:c_1\to c_2$, $v:c_2\to c_3$, and the identity-square clause gives $\gamma_1=1$. Step 1's direct-image comparisons then give $\tau_{vu}=\tau_u\tau_v$ and $\tau_1=1$.

proof.text:
The compactification category is nonempty and cofiltered, and base change acts on it, by [lem-cbc-compactifiable-cofiltered]; a compactification is part of our hypotheses. For $c,d$ choose $u:e\to c$, $v:e\to d$ and put $\rho_{d,c}=\tau_v^{-1}\tau_u:F_c\to F_d$. To check independence, choose a common refinement of two possible $e$'s. Its two induced maps to $c$, and its two induced maps to $d$, can be equalized successively by cofilteredness. At that refinement Step 3 makes both candidate expressions equal: replacing $e$ by $t:e'\to e$ replaces the expression by $(\tau_t\tau_v)^{-1}(\tau_t\tau_u)=\tau_v^{-1}\tau_u$. Cancellation also shows independence of parallel arrows. For three compactifications make these choices simultaneously; then
$$(\tau_w^{-1}\tau_v)(\tau_v^{-1}\tau_u)=\tau_w^{-1}\tau_u.$$
This is the cocycle condition, and the expression for $c=d$ is the identity. Hence the $F_c$ are canonically identified as $Rf_!$. No limit over a possibly large category is being formed: choose one compactification and use these specified pairwise comparisons.

proof.text:
For $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$, choose a compactification $d=(i,s)$ of $g$ and one of $gf$. The compatible-tower lemma [lem-cbc-compactifiable-compatible-tower] gives a compactification $(a,p)$ of $if$, a refinement of the supplied compactification of $gf$, and $V=\overline X\times_{\overline Y}Y$ with open $b:V\to\overline X$, $j:X\to V$ and proper $q:V\to Y$, satisfying $bj=a$, $qj=f$, $pb=iq$. These are compactifications $c_f=(j,q)$, $c_{gf}=(a,sp)$. Using [def-amb-etale-compact-support], define on these choices
$$\alpha^T=\bigl(Rs_*Rp_*Db_!Dj_!\xrightarrow{\sim}R(sp)_*D(bj)_!\bigr)\circ(Rs_*\Gamma_QDj_!):Rs_*Di_!Rq_*Dj_!\longrightarrow R(sp)_*Da_!.$$
All arrows are isomorphisms by [lem-amb-unbounded-proper-open-interchange], [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition] and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. Use Step 4 to compare its three candidates with arbitrary chosen candidates. The formula is the proper/open tower comparison in the question, including its open-adjunction normalization from Step 2.

proof.text:
Here is the independence calculation for $\alpha^T$. Any two towers admit a common refining tower by [lem-cbc-compactifiable-compatible-tower], so consider a refining tower $1\to2$ with proper maps $v:\overline X_1\to\overline X_2$, $u:\overline Y_1\to\overline Y_2$, $w:V_1\to V_2$. Write $Q_1,Q_2$ for their cartesian proper/open squares and abbreviate all direct-image/open composition identifications by Step 1. Set
$$A:Dj_{2!}\to Rw_*Dj_{1!},\quad D:Di_{2!}\to Ru_*Di_{1!},\quad F:Db_{2!}Rw_*\to Rv_*Db_{1!},\quad E:D(b_2j_2)_!\to Rv_*D(b_1j_1)_!,$$
each the $\Gamma$ for its indicated square. These squares have proper vertical maps by the tower lemma; they need not be cartesian. Horizontal pasting gives $E=(F Dj_{1!})(Db_{2!}A)$. Vertical pasting, applied to the rectangle from $V_1$ to $\overline Y_2$ in its two decompositions, gives
$$(Rp_{2,*}F)(\Gamma_{Q_2}Rw_*)=(Ru_*\Gamma_{Q_1})(D Rq_{1,*}).$$
Both equations are clauses of [lem-amb-unbounded-proper-open-interchange]. Now apply $Rs_{2,*}$, insert $A$ on the input, and use naturality of $\Gamma_{Q_2}$ to move this insertion past that comparison. The first displayed identity replaces the resulting $F,A$ by $E$; the second replaces the remaining two square maps. The left route is $\tau_{gf}\alpha^{T_2}$ and the right route is $\alpha^{T_1}(\tau_g\tau_f)$, where the $\tau$'s are precisely Step 3's maps. Therefore the composition square commutes with refinements. Comparing through a common tower proves independence, including independence of the maps to the original chosen compactifications by Step 4's parallel-arrow calculation.

source.place: Tag 0F7J, refinement diagram A,B,C,D,E,F and the two pasting calculations

proof.text: For $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y\to Z$, $h:Z\to T$, choose $Z\xrightarrow{i}\overline Z\xrightarrow{t}T$. Twice apply [lem-cbc-compactifiable-compatible-tower], first to $(g,h)$ and a compactification of $hg$, then to $(f,hg)$ and one of $hgf$. Obtain $Y\hookrightarrow\overline Y\xrightarrow{s}\overline Z$ and $X\hookrightarrow\overline X\xrightarrow{p}\overline Y$, with $p,s,t$ proper. The two towers provide $W=\overline Y\times_{\overline Z}Z$, open $d:Y\hookrightarrow W$, $k:W\hookrightarrow\overline Y$, proper $q:W\to Z$, and $U=\overline X\times_{\overline Y}Y$ with open $l:X\hookrightarrow U$ and proper $m:U\to Y$. Put $V=\overline X\times_{\overline Y}W$. Its projections $b:V\to\overline X$ and $r:V\to W$ are open and proper by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change, lem-pc-proper-base-change]. The projection equations and universal property in [def-pc-fibre-product] identify $U=V\times_WY$; its projection $a:U\to V$ is open by the same open base-change lemma. Thus $Q_A=(a,m,r,d)$, $Q_B=(b,r,p,k)$, $Q_C=(k,q,s,i)$ are cartesian proper/open squares. The open subschemes $U,V,W$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. This supplies all hypotheses of [lem-amb-compact-support-staircase-expansion].

proof.text: In this staircase put $\mathsf A=\Gamma_{Q_A}$, $\mathsf B=\Gamma_{Q_B}$, $\mathsf C=\Gamma_{Q_C}$, using [lem-amb-unbounded-proper-open-interchange]. The two expansion identities of [lem-amb-compact-support-staircase-expansion] identify the two iterated applications of Step 5 with its displayed $L$ and $R$, with common source $Rt_*Di_!Rq_*Dd_!Rm_*Dl_!$ and common target $Rt_*Rs_*Rp_*Db_!Da_!Dl_!$. This invokes the fixed-staircase expansion, not an associativity theorem for compact supports. Step 1 supplies the structural parentheses used in those identities.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-amb-natural-transformation-whisker-exchange] with $F=Dd_!Rm_*$, $G=Rr_*Da_!$, $H=Di_!Rq_*$, $K=Rs_*Dk_!$, $\eta=\mathsf A$ and $\theta=\mathsf C$. It gives
$$(Rs_*Dk_!\mathsf A)\circ(\mathsf C Dd_!Rm_*)=(\mathsf C Rr_*Da_!)\circ(Di_!Rq_*\mathsf A).$$
Whisker on the input by $Dl_!$, apply $Rt_*$, and postcompose with $Rt_*Rs_*\mathsf B Da_!Dl_!$. This is exactly $R=L$ in the preceding step. Step 6 transports the equality to arbitrary compactification choices. For an identity morphism choose its identity compactification; the relevant tower squares have both proper edges or both open edges identities. The identity clause of [lem-amb-unbounded-proper-open-interchange], together with Step 1, makes the comparison the identity. This proves associativity and the units.

proof.text:
Construct base change first on a compactification $c=(j,r)$ and its fibre-product base change $c_v=(j',r')$. These are compactifications and refinements base-change functorially by [lem-cbc-compactifiable-cofiltered]. Write $\bar v:\overline X'\to\overline X$. Since $A$ is finite, two of $0,1,1+1,\ldots$ coincide, so $n1_A=0$ for some $n>0$. Thus [lem-kun-proper-base-change-torsion-ring] applies to the proper $r$ and arbitrary $v$, with the unbounded mate of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange]. Let $\beta:Dj'_!v'^*\to\bar v^*Dj_!$ be the degreewise comparison of [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map]. The open-specialization in [lem-cbc-extension-zero-base-change] identifies its inverse with $\bar v^*Dj_!\to Dj'_!v'^*$: the map $\beta$ and the inverse of the comparison in that lemma both have adjunct the open-unit map under $Dj'_!\dashv j'^*$. For $\beta$, expand its composite-adjunction mate formula: the unit and counit for the base-change inverse image cancel by a triangle identity, leaving the pulled-back open unit. This is the pasting calculation of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]. Hence the adjunction bijection identifies the specified maps. Their degreewise isomorphisms descend on every complex, using exactness and the localization clauses in Step 1. Define
$$C^c_{f,v}=(Rr'_*\beta^{-1})\circ\operatorname{Ex}_{r,v,Dj_!}:v^*Rr_*Dj_!\longrightarrow Rr'_*Dj'_!v'^*.$$
Both factors are natural isomorphisms on unbounded complexes. The proper base-change theorem imposes no restriction on the residue characteristics, $v$, or the cohomological amplitude of the input.

source.place: Tag 0F7L, lemma-base-change-shriek, chosen compactification; etale-cohomology Tag 0F0C for unbounded torsion coefficients

proof.text:
For a refinement $u:c_1\to c_2$, apply the base-change equation of [lem-amb-unbounded-proper-open-interchange] to its square with proper edges $1_X,u$ and open edges $j_1,j_2$. It states that the proper/open arrow $\gamma_u$ commutes with proper exchange and the inverse degreewise open comparisons. Whisker that equation by the remaining proper direct image. The proper composition/exchange compatibility proved by taking mates in Step 1, using [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] and [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], identifies the result as
$$C^{c_1}_{f,v}\circ v^*\tau_u=(\tau_{u_v}v'^*)\circ C^{c_2}_{f,v}.$$
Thus the $C^c$ commute with every refinement comparison. Step 4, using [lem-cbc-compactifiable-cofiltered], proves agreement under pairwise comparisons independently of the common refinement. This defines $C_{f,v}$ for the compactification-independent functors.

source.place: Tag 0F7L, independence of compactification, expanded using Tag 0F7F and sites-cohomology Tag 0E46

proof.text:
For successive changes of base $Y''\xrightarrow{w}Y'\xrightarrow{v}Y$, choose $c$, then its two successive base changes. For the proper factor, [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] defines exchange as the mate of the inverse-image square; horizontal pasting in [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] gives $\operatorname{Ex}_{r,vw}=(\operatorname{Ex}_{r_v,w}\bar v^*)\circ(w^*\operatorname{Ex}_{r,v})$. For the open factor the two comparisons are the same: under the adjunction $Dj''_!\dashv j''^*$ constructed in Step 1, compare the maps in the direction $Dj''_!\to(\text{inverse image})Dj_!$ before inverting them. Both the single map and the pasted pair of maps of [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map] have adjunct the composite open unit followed by the iterated inverse-image identification. Thus those maps agree, and so do their inverses used in $C$. The units satisfy the triangle identities, and their degreewise equations descend by Step 1. Substituting these two equalities in Step 10's formula, with naturality to interchange the middle factors, yields
$$C_{f,vw}=(C_{f_v,w}v'^*)\circ w^*C_{f,v}.$$
For the identity base change, specialize the successive-base-change equation to two identity squares. The termwise inverse-image composition maps satisfy the unit laws, by upperStarComp_id_left and the coherence of mapDerivedCategory. After these unit identifications, the equation says that the exchange is idempotent. It is invertible by Step 9, so cancellation makes it the identity. In Lean, a generic identity_exchange_of_pasting lemma performs this cancellation; upperStar_comp_id_unit supplies the descended unit equation. Step 11 gives the same assertions after any compactification comparisons.

source.place: Tag 0F7L; sites-cohomology Tags 0E46 and 0E47 and degreewise open adjunction

proof.text:
Finally base-change a chosen compatible tower for $(f,g)$; [lem-cbc-compactifiable-compatible-tower] says this is again such a tower. Write $v_Z:Z'\to Z$, $v_Y:Y'\to Y$, $v_X:X'\to X$ for projections. Expand $\alpha$ by Step 5 and $C$ by Step 10. The resulting diagram has exactly three types of nontrivial factor squares: exchange with the composition of proper direct images, exchange with the composition of two open extensions, and exchange with the proper/open interchange. The first commutes by the mate-pasting calculation of Step 1 ([def-kun-unbounded-exchange, lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]); the second commutes by composing the open-unit adjuncts of Step 12, inserting the composition identification of [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition]. For the third, the required equality is precisely
$$(Rp'_*e_b)(\operatorname{Ex}_{p}Db_!)(v_{\overline Y}^*\Gamma_Q)
=(\Gamma_{Q'}v_V^*)(Di'_!\operatorname{Ex}_q)(e_iRq_*),$$
the base-change equation of [lem-amb-unbounded-proper-open-interchange] for the tower square $Q=(V,b,q,p,Y,i,\overline Y)$. Whisker this equality by the outer proper functor and the inner open extension. Composing the three factor squares and canceling the structural identifications gives the full equality
$$C_{gf,v_Z}\circ v_Z^*\alpha_{g,f}
=(\alpha_{g',f'}v_X^*)\circ(Rg'_!C_{f,v_Y})\circ(C_{g,v_Z}Rf_!).$$
Step 6 and Step 11 then give this equation for arbitrary compactification choices. This explicitly proves the composition/exchange compatibility which the proof of Tag 0F7L leaves to its three factor compatibilities.

proof.text: Check the final bounded-below normalization on actual maps. The category of module sheaves has enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives], and [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] provides bounded-below injective representatives, which are also K-injective. Exact open extension preserves the lower bound, so bounded-below resolutions can be chosen again after every open extension. Both bounded-below and unbounded $Rr_*$ are then represented by $r_*I$ on the same injective resolution, naturally in the input; equality of the induced morphisms is checked by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. On these representatives, the new $\Gamma$ of [lem-amb-unbounded-proper-open-interchange] and the bounded-below $\gamma$ of [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence] are represented by the identical map $i_!r_*J\cong p_*k_!J\to p_*I$. Thus all refinement and tower-composition maps agree with [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons]. For the proper exchange, the two constructions are the same adjunction mate: on an injective representative $I$, the derived counit is induced by the sheaf evaluation $r^*r_*I\to I$, and both inverse images and square isomorphisms are termwise. Hence the unit--square--counit formula in [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] restricts to the identical formula in [def-cbc-exchange-map]. The open factor there is the same inverse degreewise comparison by Step 10. Therefore the whole exchange restricts to the specified map of [thm-cbc-finite-torsion], and the already proved coherence equations restrict with it. This is equality of the named maps; no assertion that cohomology or stalks detect equality of derived morphisms is used.
